items.title: Presenting Rooted, a Story Not Common
items.summary: Editor’s Note: In late 2022, we sent a team of writers and photographers to Mexico. The goal of their trip was unique—to visit artist and longtime Arhaus partner, Javier, and to capture the magic happening in his workshops. Rooted is a series that tells Javier’s story: his family, his process, and his passion for the trees. Discover more. Uncommon in every instance is a pursuit of beauty that is felt, not followed. One born of passion, not pastime. It is this unconventional exploration that shapes our story. One told not in words, but in rough-hewn textures and sanded grain. In wild-found roots and windswept limbs. In the art and craft we continually seek, we find experiences that shape us as storytellers. Studies in devotion that are nearly impossible to express. Our visits to these storied studios and workspaces in Mexico have forever altered our perceptions of makers and making.Of these histories hidden, we are curious collectors. Gathering trees fallen and forgotten. Preserving their ancestry as carefully as we would our own. Listening. Considering character, vein, and voice. Observing. Admiring the influence cast by sun-soaked days and years. Seeing, in ways we haven’t before, the effects of fire and wind and water. Breathing in the energy that continues to fuel our craft.Thoughtfully re-constructed pieces. Of nature. Of time. Of culture. Of commitment. These are what we’re here to gather. Pieces that transport you, that take you, and keep you.Every day, the hum of practice and process guides our calling. Our collecting. Of nature, of pieces, of places capable and willing to create them. Just outside Mexico City, in a family of artisans, we find like minds, hearts.Uncovering ways to honor the Earth and to make it accessibly smaller. That’s what fills us. Collecting curiosity. Awe. The energy of ideas. The whir of simple machines. The quiet gratitude of a forest restored. Then sharing, with each of these, the chance to feel things and think things. This is the kind of living that we want to build rooms around. And with.And here, by the hands of many, we carry these seasons forward. Sustaining old and new. Together seeking the unexpected. And seeing, through new eyes, the beauty in imperfection and honor.

items.title: Seeing Things Differently, Together
items.summary: I first met Javier while traveling around Mexico, searching for artists, woodworkers, and craftsmen to collaborate with. Soft-spoken Javier was all three, a rare combination of imaginative dreamer and skillful doer who worked only with salvaged and naturally fallen trees. He recognized the specialness in every piece of timber, letting their natural uniqueness drive each of his designs. Where others saw imperfections—blade marks, scorching, knot holes—Javier saw characteristics to highlight. There was something different in the handcrafted pieces he was creating. They were inventive. And exceptional. And unlike anything I had seen in the American furniture market. Arhaus and Javier began working together, forming a partnership built on the shared philosophies of artisan craftsmanship, sustainable practices, and celebrating the beauty of natural materials. As our businesses grew over the years, so did our collaboration. Our senses of style evolved and refined. We developed new collections and expanded our offerings into new spaces of the home. Javier built new workshops and deepened his commitments to sustainable harvesting. He’s still working with naturally fallen trees as much as possible, and replanting his beloved forests along the way—now with his three sons and hundreds of skilled artisans working beside him. I am so honored and proud to partner with Javier, and to offer our customers the most beautiful handcrafted furniture collections in the world. I hope you enjoy our Rooted series, and find endless inspiration in the stories we’ve shared. JOHN REED, ARHAUS CO-FOUNDER

items.title: A Laboratory of Logs
Vessels
With Every Fiber, Being
items.summary: In every trace of tree, a lifetime of qualities and characteristics are worn deeply. Milpa burls and other weathered roots put their past courage and brawn on display. An exhibition of knots, splits, blemishes, and cracks. Of warping and wormholes. Each still holds tight the strength of ages and ancestry. All swirled and mottled inside. Their once-soaring reach turned inward. Condensed into intricate, lined designs. These weighty roots are quiet. Patient. Insistent that they stand apart. And that is where our ambitions align. In the uncommon. In unexpected artistry and approach. Shared here, with artisans that embrace found materials. “We design backwards,” explains Pablo, who creates heirloom furnishing alongside his father, Javier. “We let each tree reveal its intention, then we decide what to create.” Where others see imperfect, flawed, and unusable, Javier sees pliant and possible. And they do. Promising trees a forever state as meaningful and beautiful as their lives before. “Our father always says we must honor the life of the tree.” Rodrigo

items.title: Artistry Shared
items.summary: Alive in space and spirit, histories emerge. Stories of countless artisans and makers who have cast their influence. Fathers and sons, mothers, grandmothers. Each has found their place here. Sharing their artistry, their time, and their traditions, in pieces built from family trees. Mastering and teaching old-world techniques so that they will live on. Carving, cutting, finishing. Promising, to those who came before, that this craftsmanship will never be lost. Tradition paired with modern making. Welding. Turning. Sanding. Guided by touch, these powerful tools can only do what is asked of them. Not work, but works. Every day made by hand. By hands. Created by process, by practice. Each final form adorned with pride that feels visible. By countless methods and means, in this skillful preserving of ancestry and craft, generations are deeply rooted. Legacies are quietly etched, ingrained, encased in these woods and woodshops. Forever in these sculpted pieces, the spirit of centuries stays.
